hook.line: Don Hernando wants a jacket for the rainy season, and the first thing he asks is whether it can take the water. Spanish names the threat after *a*.
hook.es: Esta chaqueta es resistente al agua.

examples.es: Mi celular es resistente al agua.
Esta chaqueta es resistente al frío.
Es un vidrio a prueba de balas.

examples.en: It has great resistance to heat.

rule:
Say what something can take after *resistente a*: *resistente al agua*, *resistente al frío*. *A* plus *el* becomes *al*.

The noun form works too: *tiene mucha resistencia al calor*.

The verb *resistir* takes its object directly, with no *a*: *resiste el calor*.

For "proof against", use *a prueba de*: *a prueba de balas*.

English says "water-resistant" as one word, so Spanish needs the extra *a*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *resistente a* an adjective with a complement: the threat completes the meaning.

readAndPick.es: El cemento es resistente a la humedad.
Las ventanas no son resistentes al fuego.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El cemento es resistente ___ la humedad.* (*a* or *de*) Cement is resistant to damp.
yourTurn.answer: El cemento es resistente a la humedad.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Es resistente ___ agua.* (*a el* or *al*) It's water-resistant.
Say: My cell phone is water-resistant.
yourTurn.answer: Mi celular es resistente al agua.
Esta chaqueta es resistente al frío.
yourTurn.why: Same frame, with a different threat.

yourTurn.answer: Es un vidrio a prueba de balas.
yourTurn.why: *A prueba de* plus the thing it is proof against.
The verb *resistir* takes its object with no *a*.
Same words as the statement, with question marks.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative and plural: *La ventana es resistente al fuego.* The windows aren't fire-resistant.
yourTurn.answer: Las ventanas no son resistentes al fuego.
yourTurn.why: The adjective turns plural with *ventanas*: *no son resistentes*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The threat follows *a*, not *de*, and *a el* becomes *al*.
The verb *resistir* takes its object directly, while the adjective *resistente* needs *a*.

personal: Think of something you own that has to survive something: rain, heat, drops. Say what it is resistant to with *es resistente a…*
